derivations.claim: When $v=0$, both maps have zero source or target and hence are zero. There is one solution, stability is vacuous, and $G_0$ is trivial, so $\mathfrak M(0,1)$ is a point. Its invariant coordinate ring is $\mathbb C$, whose only prime ideal is $(0)$; hence $\mathfrak M_0(0,1)$ and the fibre $\mathcal L(0,1)$ are points by [F2]–[F3].

When $v=1$, write $I(w)=iw$ and $J(z)=jz$ for $i,j\in\mathbb C$. The moment equation is $ij=0$ and stability is $j\ne0$, so $i=0$ on the stable locus. Since $G_1=\mathbb C^\times$ sends $j$ to $jg^{-1}$ transitively on $\mathbb C^\times$, $\mathfrak M(1,1)$ is one point.

A monomial basis of $A_1=\mathbb C[i,j]/(ij)$ is $1$, $i^a$ ($a\ge1$), and $j^b$ ($b\ge1$). Under the point action $(i,j)\mapsto(gi,jg^{-1})$, evaluation of these monomials scales by $1$, $g^a$, and $g^{-b}$, respectively. The nonconstant basis monomials have pairwise distinct nonzero characters $g^a$ and $g^{-b}$; their linear independence therefore implies that an invariant polynomial has only its constant term; hence $A_1^{G_1}=\mathbb C$. Its spectrum has one point by [F3], and the image of the stable orbit is that point, so $\mathfrak M_0(1,1)$ and $\mathcal L(1,1)$ are points.

The product $\mathfrak M(0,1)\times\mathfrak M(1,1)$ is a point by steps 1.1 and 2.1. It lies in $P_{0,1}$: use $V'=0$ and the stable middle datum $(V_1,I=0,J=1)$; the inclusion is injective and the quotient has one-dimensional vertex space, zero framing space and zero induced maps, hence is $S$. Thus $P_{0,1}$ is a nonempty subset of a point, so it is a point; both projections are the unique identity map.

derivations.claim: Define $\rho(a)(h)=ah$ for $a,h\in H$. Since multiplication is $R$-bilinear, for each fixed $a$ the map $h\mapsto ah$ is $R$-linear and $a\mapsto\rho(a)$ is $R$-linear, so $\rho:H\to\operatorname{End}_R(H)$ is an $R$-linear map.

For $a,b,h\in H$, $\rho(ab)(h)=(ab)h=a(bh)=(\rho(a)\circ\rho(b))(h)$ by associativity, and $\rho(1_H)(h)=1_Hh=h$, so $\rho(1_H)=\operatorname{id}_H$. Thus $\rho$ is a unital $R$-algebra homomorphism and hence a Hall-algebra representation by [F1].

For either form and any power-sum monomial $p_\mu$ of degree $r-1$, orthogonality makes the pairing of $p_1p_\mu$ with $p_1^r$ vanish unless $\mu=(1^{r-1})$. Nondegenerate diagonal norms then force each adjoint image of $p_1^r$ to be a multiple of $p_1^{r-1}$.
